question: Does the MCP runtime manager's aggregate lease contract cover every runtime partition and use that reset/delete can retire, making final-release cleanup safe to land?
rationale: The patch and proof establish the run-lease behavior, but only an area owner can confirm that the lifecycle invariant is complete across all MCP lease-producing surfaces and intentional for gateway reset/delete.

options.title: Refresh and approve lifecycle contract
options.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun exact-head checks, and land after an MCP lifecycle owner confirms aggregate lease coverage across all runtime partitions.

options.title: Require cross-partition proof
options.body: Keep the PR open and add a focused test where multiple lease types or requester partitions drain in different orders before retirement completes.

options.title: Pause the lifecycle change
options.body: Pause this PR if the manager cannot currently guarantee complete lease accounting without broader ownership refactoring.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun exact-head checks, and land after an MCP lifecycle owner confirms aggregate lease coverage across all runtime partitions.
